c1037.summary: Tyagaraja names Rama's family as his own: Sita and Rama his parents, the great devotees his brothers and kin.
m: Sita is our mother; Sri Rama is our father.
Hanuman son of the Wind, Saumitri, Garuda, Shatrughna, Bharata and the others are our brothers, O mind.
Shiva, Vasishtha, Parashara, Narada, Shaunaka, Shuka, Indra, Gautama, Ganesha, Guha, Sanaka and the others,
and whoever are the foremost devotees on earth — all of them are Tyagaraja's dearest kin, O mind.

c1066.summary: The kingdom of devotion to Rama: rare to attain, beyond description, known only by experience.
m: The empire of devotion to Rama — which fortunate men attain it, O mind?
The very sight of such people is supreme bliss itself.
I cannot describe it as 'it is like this' — it is known only through one's own experience,
(devotion) to the Lord who created the three worlds in play, praised by Tyagaraja amid the joyous music.

c1122.summary: Tyagaraja describes a vision of Rama on the hill, served by his attendants, who promised to protect him.
m: I saw clearly Rama dwelling on the mountain,
as his attendants served him, fanning with flower fans and fly-whisks.
Thrilled, my eyes filling with tears of joy, longing to speak with him,
I saw, as in a dream, the Lord praised by Tyagaraja, who said 'In ten days I will protect you'.

c1450.summary: A string of salutations and loving reproaches to Rama, ending with his name as the daily discipline.
m: Salutations, delight of the Raghus, builder of the bridge, cool sandal-paste to devotees, O Rama.
Lord of Lakshmi, is this a quarrel with me? Am I apart from you? Does this please you, Rama?
Sri Rama, who moves in the heart, is protecting me a burden? Is it too heavy for a king, Rama?
I heard of you, I trusted you, I said 'refuge', I said 'come', Rama.
I won't swerve, I won't leave devotion, I won't beg others — I am yours, Rama.
I said 'give me fragrant betel', I said 'grant me a boon', I said 'come and speak', Rama.
Is it fair? Is this your inheritance? Am I so despicable? Is this what the sages sang of you, Rama?
Look at me, protect me, unite with us in splendour, Rama.
Well-being, the divine abode, the daily discipline — is the name of Rama, Rama.
Come quickly, ocean of compassion, dweller in Sri Tyagaraja's heart, Rama.

c2297.summary: What use are eyes, body, hands and tongue that are not used to see, embrace, worship and praise the Lord?
m: Eyes that do not fully behold the beauty of the serpent-reclining Lord, beyond the mind's grasp —
why have eyes, why have eyes, why their sparkle?
A body that does not lovingly embrace Sri Hari, whose radiance surpasses the dark rain cloud —
why a body, why a body, why this house?
Hands that do not worship him with lotus, jasmine, tulasi, viruvaji and parijata flowers —
why hands, why hands, why this household life?
A tongue that does not cherish and praise the form of Rama, who ruled Tyagaraja with love —
why a tongue, why a tongue, why a rosary?

c1087.summary: A lullaby inviting Rama to swing on the swing as gods, sages and devotees sing to him.
m: Swing on the swing, Sri Rama,
(listening to) bedtime songs, O true emperor.
As Brahma and all the gods serve you, as pure sages
meditate on you, and lovely devotees sing your virtues and alapanas,
as Narada and others praise you resplendently, as you listen to their essence,
ever protecting those who trust you, beholding the fruit of the Vedas' essence, Sri Rama,
as celestial women of fresh charm sing in detail — such is your fortune!
In the hall of nine gems, Sri Rama, who took the form praised by Tyagaraja.

c2841.summary: A prayer to Rama, the immeasurable, lover of music, praised by Narada.
m: O Raghuvara, immeasurable one, protect me.
Moon to the ocean of the Raghu race, Sri Rama, protect me.
Bee to the lotus of the Solar race, lover of music,
lord of the Solar race, praised by Narada who delights in svara, laya and murchana,
lamp on the mountain of the Solar race, whose holy feet are praised by great devotees,
Lord of Sita, praised by Tyagaraja, dear friend of the monkey chiefs, adorned with virtues.

c2532.summary: Tyagaraja tells Rama that it was Sita, by holding his hand, who made him great: she let him have the glory of slaying Ravana.
m: By taking the hand of our Janaki, you became a great king.
Best of kings, lotus-eyed one, listen: the fame that shines — 'he slew Ravana and others' —
going to the forest, never disobeying your command, she left her illusory form and stayed within the fire;
she followed the demon, stayed at the foot of the Ashoka tree, burned at his words, yet did not destroy him with a glance —
staying so, did she not make the glory yours alone, O Lord of Lakshmi, protector of Tyagaraja?

c2324.summary: Whose words have you heeded, Rama, that you will not come? Tyagaraja believed you were the devotees' servant and true to your word.
m: Whose words did you listen to? Won't you come? Are you not here? Bravo, bravo!
I cannot understand this puzzle — people on earth speak of your humanity and valour.
That you are subservient to your devotees — the words of great devotees who saw your manifest form —
I believed them true; I was happy, thinking you the all-powerful great God,
and I took you, praised by pure-minded Tyagaraja, to be true to your word on this earth.

c2685.summary: Tyagaraja calls on Ranganatha of Srirangam: when called, won't you answer and come?
m: O Ranganatha, reclining one, when I call, won't you answer 'O' and come?
Did not Shiva, by beholding you, become lord of Kailasa?
Thinking 'this is Vaikuntha on earth', you are swelling with joy within yourself;
if you remain lost in Lakshmi like this, when will our worries end?
Among people who cannot bear another's good, I suffered greatly; to see your divine form
and chest adorned with pearl strings I have come, O ornament of Tyagaraja's heart.

c2304.summary: How can one describe the good fortune of Shabari, who served Rama with fruits and attained the highest state?
m: How can I describe Shabari's good fortune?
Though the world is full of noble women of self-control,
she served Rama to her eyes' content, offered him sweet fruits, her body thrilling,
bowed at his feet, and in the presence of the lord of the Solar race attained the state of no return —
the merit of that woman, praised by Tyagaraja!

c2411.summary: Give up attainments that wane and lead to rebirth; worship of Rama is the path to the lasting abode.
m: O mind, give up the attainments that wane and lead to rebirth —
the fruits of Sanskrit drama, poetics, Vedas, Puranas, sacrifice, japa and penance.
Whatever you do, carry the Lord of the world on your head and in your heart;
worship of the one praised by Tyagaraja is the path that grants the true, lasting abode.

c2571.summary: Tyagaraja imagines Rama delighting in having made his home in Tiruvaiyaru (Panchanada) on the Kaveri, a city more beautiful than heaven.
m: Haven't you become proud and happy, Rama, praised by sages, giver of boons to the elephant king, Sri Rama?
O Supreme Person, Lord of the world, of gentle speech, treasury of jewel-like virtues — for you,
on the banks of the Kaveri, touched by the matchless Malaya breeze, with mansions and terraces,
in houses shining with beauty, where Brahmins tend the sacred fires and with Vedic chants
praise you — thinking 'I have found a fitting, beautiful city that even Shiva longs for',
with every fragrant royal flower, the sweet calls of cuckoos, praised by Shuka, Sanaka and others,
with wish-fulfilling trees, with Sarasvati serving nearby, O you whose body is like Indra's sapphire,
today, thinking 'I have a dwelling in a golden pavilion studded with nine gems',
in this world, in the beautiful Chola country, beside the noble Lord of Panchanada,
having resolved in your heart to dwell, O father of Manmatha, of name praised by Tyagaraja, whose feet Hanuman holds,
in a town that prospers in well-being, with Sita and Saumitri serving at your side.

c1721.summary: A mangalam (closing benediction): eternal victory and auspiciousness to Rama's name and form.
m: To your name and form, eternal victory and auspiciousness!
To the lotus feet held by Hanuman, son of the Wind,
to the chest adorned with fresh pearl necklaces,
to the face with a gentle smile that outshines the moon,
to your side, where lotus-eyed Sita is seated,
to you whom Prahlada, Narada and other devotees praise,
to the lotus-eyed one praised by Tyagaraja and others — (victory and auspiciousness).

c1292.summary: A morning song waking Rama at sunrise, with offerings ready and sages and kings waiting to serve.
m: Wake up, treasure of compassion; wake up, son of Dasharatha.
Wake up, treasure of compassion — it is the hour of sunrise.
I have set butter and milk in golden bowls; eat them, and protect me with your clear eyes.
Narada and the sages, Brahma and Shiva who wears the moon wait to serve in your presence.
Kings and the guardians of the directions have all come, O king; praised by Tyagaraja, protect me.

c1430.summary: Tyagaraja recalls how Vishnu rushed to save Gajendra, Draupadi and Ramadasa, and asks why he must remain in worry.
m: O you who recline on the ocean of milk, must you keep me in worry, Rama?
I have heard how swiftly you came to save the king of elephants, Rama.
I heard how you gave garments to the jewel among women long ago; I heard how you freed brave Ramadasa from prison.
I have heard of your fame in crossing the ocean for lotus-eyed Sita; O one whose name saves, praised by Tyagaraja, rule me with compassion, Rama.

c2701.summary: A prayer to Kamakshi of Kanchipuram to protect the singer as lovingly as she protects her son Vinayaka.
m: Protect me as you protect Vinayaka; who among the gods is like you, Mother?
Protector of the helpless, Sri Kamakshi, remover of the sins of the good, Shankari, Mother!
Even as you grant boons to the lowliest of men, Brahmins and gods praise you;
can I not attain (your grace)? Won't you look on me with compassion, O queen of Kanchipura?
For the good of the world, Brahma prayed to you; though you are patient,
you took incarnation — I cannot bear any more delay, O remover of the sorrows of those who bow.
Quickly, with compassion, grant us lasting fortune and protect us, O sovereign one,
sister of Vishnu, who rules the lotus of Tyagaraja's heart, Parashakti — (protect) me.

c2578.summary: Tyagaraja answers those who speak ill of him: he never sought wealth, power or flattery, only Rama's worship.
m: People speak ill of me, O one praised by the Vedas, saying I broke up the family.
I did think that the pleasures of Manmatha's world melt away like snow;
but did I divide and hoard wealth and say 'who is my equal', or that there is no other refuge?
I longed for daily festive worship of you; in my mind the household was one;
did I, unable to bear others' prosperity day after day, say it must be split in two?
I held my life cheap and honour high, O Sri Rama, ocean of supreme bliss;
did I take a path unknown in the Lord's lineage, and flatter others to fill my belly?
Long-armed Lord of Janaki, lotus-eyed, whose feet Tyagaraja praises,
who protects without pretext those who worship you in this world — good king, I am yours.

c2751.summary: Drinking the nectar of the Ramayana story is equal to ruling a kingdom; it grants every goal of life.
m: Drinking the nectar of Rama's story is like ruling a kingdom —
(the story of) Sita, jewel among women, with Saumitri, Bharata and the rest, shining on the earth.
It grants all the fruits beginning with dharma, O mind; it is the home of courage, bliss and happiness;
it is the boat across the burning ocean of karma's bonds; it destroys the evils of Kali — (the story of) the Lord praised by Tyagaraja.

c1377.summary: How Vishvamitra must have rejoiced to see young Rama's curls dance as he defeated Maricha and broke Shiva's bow.
m: Seeing his curls swaying, how that great sage must have rejoiced!
When, surpassing in brilliance, he crushed Maricha's pride,
when, understanding the sage's glance, he broke Shiva's bow —
at that moment, (seeing the curls) shining on the face of the one praised by Tyagaraja.

c2576.summary: Rama is the nectar of nada in human form; his bow, its strings and arrows are the elements of music.
m: The nectar of nada has taken a human form here on earth, O mind —
(nada) that is the foundation of the Vedas, Puranas, Agamas and Shastras.
The seven svaras are its bells; the noble raga is the Kodanda bow; the dura, naya and
deshya styles are its three strings; the steady gait is its arrow; the graceful sangatis and phrases
are its words — the fortune of worship on earth, which Tyagaraja serves.

c2231.summary: Tyagaraja teases Rama for his broken promises: what joy does he get from telling so many lies?
m: What happiness do you gain by telling so many lies?
Time passes, but words remain, Kalyana Rama — with me,
'When I am your mother and father, why fear?' — how many promises you made;
and among your equals on earth you boasted of protecting so many, winning the elders' praise — (yet) with Tyagaraja (you lie).
